postconditions.description: The total number of rules is 4n.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= a_i, b_i, c_i <= n for a_i, b_i, c_i in rules)
postconditions.description: Each server number a_i, b_i, c_i is between 1 and n.

postconditions.expression: all(rule in rules for rule in rules)
postconditions.description: Each rule is applied exactly once.

postconditions.expression: all(rule[0] in range(1, n+1) for rule in rules)
postconditions.description: Each server number a_i in the rules is a valid server number.

postconditions.expression: all(rule[1] in range(1, n+1) for rule in rules)
postconditions.description: Each server number b_i in the rules is a valid server number.

postconditions.expression: all(rule[2] in range(1, n+1) for rule in rules)
postconditions.description: Each server number c_i in the rules is a valid server number.

postconditions.expression: all(rule[1] != rule[2] for rule in rules)
postconditions.description: Each rule specifies two different servers for replication.

postconditions.expression: all(rule[0] != rule[1] and rule[0] != rule[2] for rule in rules)
postconditions.description: The original server a_i in each rule is different from the replication servers b_i and c_i.

postconditions.expression: all(rule[1] != rule[2] for rule in rules)
postconditions.description: The replication servers b_i and c_i in each rule are different.

postconditions.expression: all(rule[1] != rule[0] and rule[2] != rule[0] for rule in rules)
postconditions.description: The original server a_i in each rule is different from the replication servers b_i and c_i.

postconditions.expression: all(rule[1] != rule[2] for rule in rules)
postconditions.description: The replication servers b_i and c_i in each rule are different.
The result is either 'YES' or 'NO' indicating whether a valid order exists.

postconditions.expression: result == 'YES' ==> len(order) == 4 * n and set(order) == set(range(1, 4 * n + 1))
postconditions.description: If the result is 'YES', the order contains all numbers from 1 to 4n exactly once.
If the result is 'NO', the order is None.
